name: Zapier
tagline: Automation platform with developer CLI, API requests, and MCP.
shortDescription: Zapier connects thousands of apps and exposes developer docs, platform CLI, custom API requests, and MCP access.
agentSummary: Agents can trigger broad SaaS actions through curated Zapier connectors, which is powerful but needs strict action review.
bestFor: Cross-app automations, long-tail SaaS integrations, and workflow prototyping.
cautionNotes: Key limitations: Zapier can mutate many external systems; use allowlists, approval gates, and least-privilege connections. Verify official docs, pricing, rate limits, permissions, and production side effects before delegating account-changing actions to an agent. MCP servers inherit the connected account's scopes and may send prompts or data to third-party services; configure read-only or narrow scopes when available. CLI access is powerful but can run destructive local or production commands; prefer dry runs, preview environments, and non-production credentials.
pricingSummary: Public task-based pricing with free and paid plans.
authModel: Zapier account auth, connected app OAuth, per-server tool configuration, and MCP client auth.
browserSupport: Editor UI is important for reviewing actions and connections.

capabilities.detail: Zapier SDK CLI supports custom integrations and API requests.
Zapier MCP connects agents to thousands of app integrations and user-configured actions through Zapier-managed authentication.
Docs include SDK, CLI, app building, and AI/MCP guidance.
Task and plan pricing are public.
Editor UI is important for reviewing actions and connections.
The tool has documented test, local, preview, self-hosted, or staging paths that let agents validate changes away from production.
